Where the ball passed, not one of us precisely knew; but I fancy it must have been over our heads, and that the wind of it may have contributed to our disaster.

At any rate, the boat sank by the stern, quite gently, in three feet of water, leaving the captain and myself, facing each other, on our feet. The other three took complete headers, and came up again, drenched and bubbling.

So far there was no great harm. No lives were lost, and we could wade ashore in safety. But there were all our stores at the bottom, and, to make things worse, only two guns out of five remained in a state for service. Mine I had snatched from my knees and held over my head, by a sort of instinct.

He recalls the sinking with lasting terror and shame at his own panic.
He blames the captain angrily for steering the boat into danger.

g.passage:
"See, Winter comes, to rule the varied year,
Sullen and sad, with all his rising train,
Vapours, and clouds, and storms. Be these my theme,
These! that exalt the soul to solemn thought,
And heavenly musing. Welcome, kindred glooms!
Congenial horrors, hail! with frequent foot,
Pleased have I, in my cheerful morn of life,
When nursed by careless Solitude I lived,
And sung of Nature with unceasing joy,
Pleased have I wander'd through your rough domain;
Trod the pure virgin-snows, myself as pure;
Heard the winds roar, and the big torrents burst;
Or seen the deep-fermenting tempest brew'd
In the grim evening sky. Thus passed the time,
Till through the lucid chambers of the south
Look'd out the joyous Spring, look'd out, and smiled!"
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude in the text?
options: He dreads winter's arrival and longs only for the return of spring.
He treats winter with indifference, since it no longer affects him.
He welcomes winter's storms as kindred companions that lift the soul.
He regrets ever having wandered through winter's harsh domain.

g.passage:
The night was cloudy and black, and every line in the architecture of the largest building in the world was defined in light, even to the cross, which, as I have said before, is at the height of a mountain from the base. For about an hour it was a delicate but vast structure of shining lines, like a drawing of a glorious temple on the clouds. At eight, as the clock struck, flakes of fire burst from every point, and the whole building seemed started into flame. It was done by a simultaneous kindling of torches in a thousand points, a man stationed at each. The glare seemed to exceed that of noonday. No description can give an idea of it.

I am not sure that I have not been a little tedious in describing the ceremonies of the holy week.

g.passage: Not that it must be for a moment supposed that our Women are destitute of affection. But unfortunately the passion of the moment predominates, in the Frail Sex, over every other consideration. This is, of course, a necessity arising from their unfortunate conformation. For as they have no pretensions to an angle, being inferior in this respect to the very lowest of the Isosceles, they are consequently wholly devoid of brain-power, and have neither reflection, judgment nor forethought, and hardly any memory. Hence, in their fits of fury, they remember no claims and recognize no distinctions.

g.explanation: 서술자는 여성이 애정이 없는 것은 아니지만 순간의 감정이 다른 모든 고려를 압도한다고 말한다. 그 이유를 각이 없는 몸의 구조 때문에 판단력과 기억력이 없다는 데서 찾으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 비교 주장이 없고, B의 특정 사건과 D의 이등변삼각형 비판은 지문의 요지가 아니다.

excerpt.text: Not that it must be for a moment supposed that our Women are destitute of affection. But unfortunately the passion of the moment predominates, in the Frail Sex, over every other consideration. This is, of course, a necessity arising from their unfortunate conformation. For as they have no pretensions to an angle, being inferior in this respect to the very lowest of the Isosceles, they are consequently wholly devoid of brain-power, and have neither reflection, judgment nor forethought, and hardly any memory. Hence, in their fits of fury, they remember no claims and recognize no distinctions.

g.passage:
In the end she rejected both courses and decided for the riding costume. The reason she gave for this decision--the reason she gave herself--was that the riding costume would invest the call with an air of accident, of impulse. The real reason.

It may be that some feminine reader can guess why she chose the most startling, the most gracefully becoming, the most artlessly physical apparel in her wardrobe.

She said nothing to her father at lunch about her plans. Why should she speak of them? He might oppose; also, she might change her mind. After lunch she set out on her usual ride, galloping away into the hills--but she had put twenty-five dollars in bills in her trousers pocket.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: It shows a woman openly arguing with her father about her plans.
It shows the narrator criticizing the woman's choice of clothing.
It describes an ordinary ride taken purely for exercise in the hills.
It reveals a woman's concealed motives and quiet preparations for a call.
g.explanation: 그녀는 승마복을 고르며 '우연한 방문처럼 보이려고'라는 이유를 스스로에게 대지만, 서술자는 '진짜 이유'가 따로 있음을 암시한다. 또 아버지에게 계획을 말하지 않고 평소처럼 말을 타러 나가면서 몰래 돈을 챙기므로 D가 정답이다. A는 아버지와 말다툼하지 않았고, B와 C는 지문의 의도를 놓친다.

g.passage:
Every hand was hard at work over its appointed task, and there was no evidence in that silent well-ordered hive, of the recent little revolution.

When the mathematician, having made his way to his own work-bench, had passed his unerring hand over it, he found all as he had left it—not a thing disturbed; every tool, every scrap of metal, every morsel of wire lying intact. Even the little steel coil which had come to such sudden grief, had been carefully rewound into proper compass, and placed ready to hand by Isaac Habrecht. “It is correctly adjusted, I think?” he said, as Dasipodius took it up.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: It shows the workshop restored to order, with even the damage quietly mended.
It depicts a revolt in the workshop that is still spreading among workers.
It describes the mathematician's anger on discovering his tools missing.
It reveals that Isaac Habrecht damaged the steel coil on purpose.
g.explanation: 지문은 조용한 작업장에 최근의 작은 '혁명'의 흔적이 전혀 없다고 말한다. 수학자가 작업대를 살펴보니 모든 것이 그대로였고, 망가졌던 코일까지 다시 감겨 준비되어 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 이미 끝난 소동을 진행 중이라 보고, C와 D는 지문 내용과 반대된다.
